Entender o que é advérbio (a palavra que: Understand what an adverb is (the word that never changes), form adverbs from adjectives and ask questions.
Advérbio: a palavra que nunca muda: The adverb: the word that never changes
Advérbio é a palavra que informa COMO, Q: An adverb is a word that tells you HOW, WHEN, WHERE or HOW MUCH something happens: «well», «today», «here», «very». It never changes its form, not for gender and not for plural. That is the difference from the adjective: «хороший дом» (adjective: it changes with the noun) × «Он хорошо работает» (adverb: always «хорошо»). Many adverbs are born from an adjective: drop the ending (-ый, -ий, -ой) and add -о. Others are words in their own right: здесь, там, сейчас, очень, всегда.
«bom» → «bem», «lento» → «lentamente». O: «quick» → «quickly», «slow» → «slowly». The idea is the same as in English: the adverb comes from the adjective and does not vary. In English you add -ly; in Russian you just swap the ending for -о.
Depois de um verbo, use o advérbio, que: After a verb, use the adverb, which does not change.
Para dizer COMO alguém faz algo, use adv: To say HOW someone does something, use an adverb.
Say: «Я хорошо читаю. Он плохо говорит. Она быстро работает.»

Os advérbios de frequência formam uma es: The adverbs of frequency form a scale: всегда (always), часто (often), иногда (sometimes), редко (rarely), никогда (never). In Russian, when «никогда» is there, the verb takes «не» as well: «Я никогда не читаю», literally «I never don't read». In English we say just «I never read». This is called the double negative, and in Russian it is compulsory.
o português também aceita «não ... nunca: Non-standard English also stacks negatives («I don't never read»), but in Russian this is the standard rule: «не» is always required.
